description:
Goal

Encode a value from one valid partial tuple transport shape into another contextual partial tuple shape by positional reprojection, without materializing tuple fields that the destination explicitly ignores.

Signal

The reactive RuntimeDemand cutover exposes a latent encoder limitation on 00420 and a minimal make/consume structured-return program. Producer layout is Tuple([Nothing, Tuple([Lane, Lane, Lane])]) with Absent outer carrier; consumer layout is Tuple([Nothing, Lane(inner_tuple)]) with Absent outer carrier. They have the same runtime tuple arity and the same semantic demand TupleFields([Ignore, Whole]), but intentionally different physical layouts. The exact CallArg to ExecutableInput relation is present and both artifacts are fresh. Backend and native encoders compare ShapeIds, then materialize the whole source when they differ; that necessarily reads the intentionally absent ignored tag.

These shapes are not denotational duplicates and must not be unified globally: one value may have several contextual consumers. This is not a stale product, missing demand edge, Ty-string/equivalence problem, or justification for Whole widening.

Strategy

Put contextual reprojection at the existing tuple view/encoding boundary shared in concept by backend and native paths. When source and destination are tuple shapes of the same runtime arity, split the runtime value using the source shape's positional spans, discard any field whose destination shape is Nothing, and recursively encode every other source field into the corresponding destination field. If a required destination field cannot be constructed from its corresponding source field, retain the existing hard failure. Do not materialize the outer source tuple or mutate transport facts.

TDD and acceptance

- First add focused RED tests for backend and native encoding with source Tuple([Nothing, Tuple([three present lanes])]) and destination Tuple([Nothing, Lane(inner tuple)]). Both must produce the inner tuple ValueRef without reading or fabricating the ignored tag.
- A destination Nothing safely discards a present or Absent source field.
- A non-Nothing destination field paired with an unconstructible/Absent source field still fails; no value is invented.
- Equal source/destination layouts retain their existing fast path, and non-tuple or arity-mismatched conversions retain current behavior.
- Multiple contextual consumers may request distinct destination layouts without changing the producer's layout or each other's answers.
- Backend interpreter and native/AOT encoders remain behaviorally concordant under focused contract tests.
- After stacking beneath fz-kdt.4, the minimal make/consume program and 00420_enum_take_drop_split pass interp, run, and build+execute with exact partial RuntimeDemand; no sticky cone Whole is required.
- Full focused transport/backend/native suites, determinism, formatting, check, strict clippy, and warnings-as-errors pass.

Removal

Delete any whole-source materialization branch made redundant for same-arity tuple reprojection and all temporary shape/LLDB diagnostics. Add no compatibility shim, parallel shape authority, global layout unification, semantic widening, Ty display comparison, or consumer coercion.
title: Reproject partial tuple transport without materializing erased fields
